articles.title: Glucosamine Consumption is Linked to Increased Dementia Risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: An analysis of health records from thousands of patients found an association between glucosamine consumption and higher dementia risk. The study focused on people diagnosed with neurological disorders and reports correlation, not proof that glucosamine causes dementia.

articles.title: Dementia risk factors look different around the world, large study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A USC-led study of more than 214,000 older adults across 14 countries and regions found that controllable dementia risk factors vary widely by place. The findings suggest that prevention strategies may need to be tailored locally rather than based on a single global risk profile.

articles.title: Alzheimer's tau protein has a surprising secret role in memory
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported in a mouse study that tau helps turn new experiences into lasting memories by organizing memory-storing cells. The work also suggests that abnormal tau may disrupt memory formation and recall in ways relevant to Alzheimer's disease, but the findings are preclinical.

articles.title: New study provides first evidence of dopamine system injury in the brain of long COVID patients
articles.summary_3_sentences: A brain imaging study led by CAMH researchers found evidence that long COVID is associated with injury to dopamine-releasing neurons. The finding may help explain symptoms such as fatigue-related lack of motivation, slowed movement, and memory difficulties, while pointing to possible treatment research directions.

articles.title: Study Found Teen Cannabis Use Interferes with the Brain's Reward System
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study published in Neuropsychopharmacology reported an association between adolescent cannabis use and alterations in the brain's reward system. The article describes changes in neural pathways related to reward processing and frames the findings as evidence of potential risks from teen cannabis exposure.

articles.title: Scientists discover how the brain rewires itself to truly multitask
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that extensive practice can reorganize brain activity so learned tasks rely less on the prefrontal cortex and more on specialized circuits. The findings suggest training may free cognitive resources for performing another task at the same time.

articles.title: The same sounds are mapped similarly in the human and mouse brain, study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A neuroscience study reports that similar sounds are mapped in comparable ways in human and mouse brains. The work relates to how brains organize sensory inputs into internal representations rather than processing each experience in isolation.

articles.title: Do your dreams have smells? New study on 'blind minds' reveals vast differences in imagination
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study on imagination describes large differences in people's ability to generate imagined sensations, including visual and other sensory experiences. The article highlights that inner mental experiences vary more widely than commonly assumed.

articles.title: Demystifying the molecular mechanisms of general anesthesia
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers at Weill Cornell Medicine and Birkbeck identified a site where a commonly used anesthetic binds to sodium ion channels. The finding offers a molecular explanation for how inhaled anesthetics reduce neuronal signaling and help produce unconsciousness and immobility during surgery.

topic_groups.topic: Infectious Disease, Antimicrobial Resistance, and Outbreaks

articles.title: A COVID-19 Preventive Strategy is Now FDA Approved
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that a COVID-19 preventive strategy has received FDA approval. Details in the provided record are limited, but the item concerns ongoing efforts to prevent COVID-19 after the pandemic's global impact.

articles.title: Bacterial responses to plasma may forecast mild vs severe COVID-19
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes biotechnology research using living organisms for information processing. It reports that bacterial responses to plasma may help distinguish mild from severe COVID-19, though the provided summary gives limited methodological detail.

articles.title: Artemisinin resistance is rising in East Africa--leaving anti-malarials at risk of failure
articles.summary_3_sentences: Imperial College London researchers reported that resistance to artemisinin, a key component of front-line malaria treatments, is spreading across East Africa. The study in The Lancet Infectious Diseases maps this rise and warns that current treatments could lose effectiveness if resistance continues to expand.

articles.title: Another tick-borne disease to avoid: Anaplasmosis in Canada
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Canadian Medical Association Journal practice article highlights anaplasmosis as an important tick-borne disease in Canada. The article notes that it is the country's second-most common tick-borne disease and can cause complications including myocarditis.

articles.title: Cyclosporiasis: This Parasitic Illness is Causing an Explosive Problem
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses cyclosporiasis, an illness caused by the parasite Cyclospora. The provided summary indicates the disease has been in the news and can cause gastrointestinal illness, but gives limited additional detail.

articles.title: How to stay safe and still enjoy produce this summer with the outbreak of diarrhea-causing parasite
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that a parasite often linked to contaminated fresh produce has sickened scores of people in the United States. It focuses on practical ways to reduce risk while continuing to eat fruits and vegetables during the summer.

articles.title: Proteins Help Deadly Pathogen Evade Immunity
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes proteins that help the pathogen causing louse-borne relapsing fever evade immune responses. Louse-borne relapsing fever is an acute bacterial infection marked by recurring high fever.

articles.title: A Natural Antifungal Mechanism is Revealed
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports on a natural antifungal mechanism related to Aspergillus fumigatus, a common environmental fungus that many people inhale. Details are limited, but the item concerns host or biological defenses against fungal exposure.

articles.title: Inhibiting protein to treat myeloproliferative neoplasms shows preclinical promise
articles.summary_3_sentences: St. Jude Children's Research Hospital scientists found that inhibiting menin showed promise in preclinical models of myeloproliferative neoplasms. The approach extended survival and reversed multiple disease features in the models, according to findings published in Cancer Cell.

articles.title: Novel microenvironment-targeted therapy for bone marrow recovery after injury
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes a microenvironment-targeted therapy aimed at helping bone marrow recover after injury. The context is myelosuppression after radiation or chemotherapy, which can deplete hematopoietic stem cells and sometimes require stem cell transplantation.

articles.title: Gene Therapy Improves Stem Cell Transplant Success
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that gene therapy may improve the success of stem cell transplants. It describes potential improvements in engraftment and outcomes, with relevance to oncology and transplant treatment strategies.

articles.title: Second prostate-specific membrane antigen PET scan can change treatment for nearly half of prostate cancer patients
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study in The Journal of Nuclear Medicine found that a second PSMA PET scan changed treatment plans for nearly half of prostate cancer patients whose first scan was negative. Repeat scans identified local and distant disease that affected clinical management.

articles.title: Breast cancer is rising fast in Asian American women, study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A UC San Francisco-led study reported a rapid rise in invasive breast cancer among Asian American women over the last two decades. The article frames the trend as alarming and relevant to cancer surveillance and prevention.

articles.title: Economic evaluation supports prophylactic naldemedine for opioid-induced constipation in cancer palliative care
articles.summary_3_sentences: An economic evaluation supports using prophylactic naldemedine to manage opioid-induced constipation in cancer palliative care. The article notes that opioids remain essential for advanced cancer pain but can reduce quality of life through constipation and complicate pain management.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden heart valve risk linked to gum disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that bacteria associated with gum disease may contribute to calcific aortic valve stenosis by promoting inflammation and calcium buildup in the valve. The findings are described as early and suggest a possible link between oral health and heart valve disease risk.

articles.title: Bacteria from gum disease may cause inflammation, harden heart valves
articles.summary_3_sentences: Preliminary independent research presented at an American Heart Association meeting reported that gum disease bacteria may spur calcium buildup in the aortic valve. The work links oral bacteria with inflammation and a serious form of heart valve disease, but the report is preliminary.

articles.title: Oxalate buildup triggers systemic inflammation and cardiac damage, study shows
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study reports that oxalate accumulation in chronic kidney disease can promote systemic inflammation and cardiac damage. The article explains that oxalate is normally excreted by the kidneys but can build up when kidney function is impaired.

articles.title: First E-STAR annual report offers unprecedented view of early access to kidney transplantation
articles.summary_3_sentences: The first E-STAR annual report provides a detailed view of early access to kidney transplantation in the United States. The article notes that many people with end-stage kidney disease remain on dialysis because of organ shortages and barriers across the transplant process.

articles.title: Forget GLP-1s--GLP-3s show promise in phase 3 weight loss and diabetes trial
articles.summary_3_sentences: Phase 3 TRANSCEND-T2D-1 trial results published in The Lancet reported that investigational once-weekly retatrutide improved blood sugar levels and produced substantial weight loss in adults with Type 2 diabetes. Participants were not taking diabetes medicines and had inadequate control with diet and exercise alone.

articles.title: Night owls eat later, choose less nutritious food, carry more belly fat and show higher metabolic risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported that people with a night-owl chronotype tend to eat later, choose less nutritious foods, carry more abdominal fat, and show higher metabolic risk. The article frames chronotype as a biological preference in sleep-wake timing rather than simply a lifestyle choice.

articles.title: Gene discovery may unlock infertility, early menopause clues
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports a gene discovery that may offer clues about infertility and early menopause. It connects the finding to age-related loss of ovarian eggs and follicles, which contributes to declining fertility, irregular cycles, and menopause.

articles.title: What to know about menopause: Latest guidance to empower women
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reviews current guidance on menopause, a normal life stage marking the end of reproductive years. It notes that more than four out of five women may experience symptoms that can substantially affect daily life.

topic_groups.topic: Therapeutics, Drug Discovery, and Biomedical Engineering

articles.title: Body's own cell-to-cell messaging packets studied as the basis for next-generation medicines
articles.summary_3_sentences: The Blood and Tissue Bank is studying how to manufacture and use extracellular vesicles as potential next-generation medicines. These cell-released nanoparticles carry biological information and are involved in tissue regeneration and modulation of inflammation.

articles.title: How AI accelerates radiopharmaceutical drug discovery, optimizes personalized dosimetry
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Journal of Medical Internet Research news and perspectives article describes the use of deep learning and generative AI in radiopharmaceutical medicine. It focuses on accelerating drug design and optimizing personalized dosimetry for precision cancer therapy.

articles.title: Engineers develop AI tool to design peptides that turn signals on or off
articles.summary_3_sentences: Engineers developed an AI tool to design peptides that can turn biological signals on or off. The article places the work in the broader context of using AI to generate peptide candidates and predict their properties, including for drug development.

articles.title: Scientists improve the analgesic efficacy of morphine
articles.summary_3_sentences: University of Malaga researchers reported that activation of the dopamine D4 receptor enhances morphine's analgesic effect and prevents development of morphine tolerance. The study, published in The Journal of Pain, is described as a step toward more effective pain treatments with fewer tolerance-related limitations.

articles.title: This ultrasound treatment may help stop arthritis before it starts
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers at The University of Alabama in Huntsville found that continuous low-intensity ultrasound encouraged macrophages to shift from an inflammatory state toward a tissue-repair state. The noninvasive approach is described as a potential way to help injured joints heal and reduce damaging inflammation, but the report does not establish clinical use.

topic_groups.topic: Immunology, Inflammation, and Oral Health Mechanisms

articles.title: Novel Proteins Regulate Immune Cell Exhaustion
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports the discovery of novel proteins that regulate T cell exhaustion. Because T cells help identify and target infections, the findings may inform research on mechanisms to improve immune responses.

articles.title: How studying oral inflammatory diseases can help researchers understand other human diseases
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers from VCU Massey Comprehensive Cancer Center, the VCU School of Dentistry, and the University of Pennsylvania published a Nature Communications study on oral inflammatory diseases. The work examines why some oral inflammatory diseases progress more rapidly than others and may provide broader insight into human inflammatory disease.

articles.title: Normal oxygen levels can miss severe breathlessness driven by carbon dioxide
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study led by UC Riverside biomedical scientist Erica Heinrich highlights that normal oxygen levels may miss severe dyspnea driven by carbon dioxide. The work, published in Respiratory Physiology & Neurobiology, focuses on detection and treatment gaps in breathing distress, particularly for ventilated patients.

articles.title: Emergency doctors are stressed out--and patient irritation plays a significant role
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that emergency physicians experience substantial stress and that patient irritation is a significant contributor. It places the finding in the context of growing public attention to the emotional toll of emergency medicine.

articles.title: Online therapy lowers depression and anxiety for dementia caregivers after six months
articles.summary_3_sentences: A University of East Anglia project tested a digital therapy platform for caregivers of people with dementia in nearly 500 volunteers. The online intervention was reported to lower depression and anxiety after six months.

articles.title: People have been fermenting food for millennia. Here's why more people are focused on gut health now
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses rising public interest in gut health, including fermented foods, fiber-focused diets, and personalized microbiome treatments. It also notes that concern about colorectal cancer in younger adults has contributed to attention on digestive health.

articles.title: Spaceflight Linked to Accelerated Aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports on a GeroScience study examining whether long-term spaceflight affects aging. The findings suggest an association between spaceflight and accelerated aging, with implications for astronaut health and future missions.

articles.title: Deep-sea life has a secret food source scientists never expected
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists found that extreme deep-sea pressure can squeeze nutrients from sinking organic particles, creating an unexpected food source for ocean microbes. The finding may affect understanding of deep-ocean ecosystems and Earth's carbon storage.
